topics.label: npm
topics.desc: The default Node.js package manager and CLI, bundled with Node, used to install dependencies, run scripts, and publish packages to the public or a private registry.

topics.label: Yarn
topics.desc: An alternative package manager that popularized lockfiles and workspaces; Yarn Berry adds Plug'n'Play, zero-installs, and a plugin system beyond classic node_modules.

topics.label: pnpm
topics.desc: A fast, disk-efficient package manager that hard-links a global content-addressable store and uses a strict symlinked node_modules to prevent phantom dependencies.

topics.label: package.json
topics.desc: The manifest declaring a project's metadata, dependencies, scripts, exports, and engine constraints; the entry point every Node tool reads to understand the package.

topics.label: Semantic Versioning
topics.desc: The major.minor.patch convention plus range operators (^, ~) that lets dependency ranges signal breaking changes, features, and fixes for safe automated upgrades.

topics.label: Lockfiles
topics.desc: Auto-generated files (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml) pinning the exact resolved dependency tree so installs are deterministic and reproducible across machines.

topics.label: node_modules
topics.desc: The local directory where installed dependencies live, resolved by Node's algorithm and laid out flat, nested, or symlinked; the install target for dependencies and devDependencies.

topics.label: npx & Runners
topics.desc: Tools that execute a package's binary without a global install, fetching on demand: npx for npm, plus pnpm dlx and yarn dlx equivalents for scaffolding and one-off CLIs.

topics.label: Module Bundling
topics.desc: Walking an import graph to combine ES/CommonJS modules and assets like CSS, images, and fonts into optimized, hashed bundles; the core job of webpack, Vite, and zero-config Parcel.

topics.label: Vite
topics.desc: A modern build tool serving source over native ESM with instant startup in dev and bundling via Rollup/Rolldown for production; the default for React, Vue, and Svelte apps.

topics.label: webpack
topics.desc: The long-dominant, highly configurable bundler with a vast loader and plugin ecosystem; origin of code splitting and module federation, now succeeded by the Rust-based Turbopack.

topics.label: esbuild
topics.desc: An extremely fast bundler and minifier written in Go, used directly and as the under-the-hood dependency pre-bundler and transpiler inside tools like Vite.

topics.label: Rollup
topics.desc: A bundler focused on ES modules and clean, tree-shaken output, ideal for publishing libraries; powers Vite's production build and influenced the modern bundler design.

topics.label: Tree-Shaking
topics.desc: Dead-code elimination that drops unused ES module exports from the final bundle, relying on static import analysis and sideEffects hints to shrink shipped JavaScript.

topics.label: Code Splitting
topics.desc: Breaking a bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand via dynamic import(), so the browser fetches only the code a route or interaction needs.

topics.label: Dev Server & HMR
topics.desc: The local development server with Hot Module Replacement that swaps changed modules into the running app without a full reload, preserving state for fast feedback.

topics.label: Babel
topics.desc: The classic JavaScript compiler that transforms modern and JSX syntax into widely supported code via a plugin/preset pipeline, long the standard for transpilation.

topics.label: SWC
topics.desc: A Rust-based compiler that transpiles and minifies JavaScript and TypeScript far faster than Babel, now powering Next.js, Jest transforms, and many modern toolchains.

topics.label: TypeScript Compiler (tsc)
topics.desc: The official TypeScript compiler that type-checks code and emits JavaScript and declaration files, configured through tsconfig.json's compiler options and module settings.

topics.label: PostCSS
topics.desc: A tool that transforms CSS through JavaScript plugins, enabling Autoprefixer, nesting, and future-syntax support; the engine many CSS frameworks build their pipeline on.

topics.label: Polyfills
topics.desc: Runtime shims like core-js that supply missing APIs (Promise, fetch) in older environments, complementing syntax transpilation so new features run on old engines.

topics.label: Browserslist
topics.desc: A shared config declaring which browsers a project supports, read by Babel, Autoprefixer, and bundlers to decide which transforms and prefixes are actually needed.

topics.label: Source Maps
topics.desc: Mapping files that link compiled, bundled, or minified output back to original source, letting debuggers and error reporters show real file names and line numbers.

topics.label: ESLint
topics.desc: The dominant pluggable JavaScript/TypeScript linter that flags bugs and enforces code style via configurable rules, shareable configs, and a rich plugin ecosystem.

topics.label: Prettier
topics.desc: An opinionated code formatter that reprints source to a consistent style automatically, ending formatting debates and typically run on save or in pre-commit hooks.

topics.label: EditorConfig
topics.desc: A simple .editorconfig file that enforces basic whitespace and charset settings across editors and IDEs, keeping indentation and line endings consistent for every contributor.

topics.label: Stylelint
topics.desc: A linter for CSS, SCSS, and CSS-in-JS that catches errors and enforces conventions in stylesheets, the Prettier/ESLint counterpart for the styling layer.

topics.label: Git Hooks (Husky)
topics.desc: Scripts triggered by Git events, commonly managed with Husky or simple-git-hooks, used to run linting, formatting, and tests automatically before commits or pushes.

topics.label: lint-staged
topics.desc: A tool that runs linters and formatters only on Git-staged files, making pre-commit checks fast by avoiding a full-project scan on every commit.

topics.label: Commit Linting
topics.desc: Enforcing structured commit messages with commitlint against the Conventional Commits spec, enabling automated changelogs and semantic-release versioning downstream.

topics.label: VS Code
topics.desc: The dominant code editor, extensible via a huge marketplace, with integrated Git, debugging, terminal, IntelliSense, and remote/devcontainer support for full-stack work.

topics.label: Editors & IDEs
topics.desc: The broader landscape of development environments, from Neovim and the JetBrains IDEs to AI-first editors like Cursor and Zed, each trading off speed and integration.

topics.label: Terminal & Shells
topics.desc: The command-line environment built on shells like bash, zsh, and fish running in a terminal emulator, the primary surface for running tools and scripting workflows.

topics.label: CLI Proficiency
topics.desc: Fluency with core Unix utilities and pipes (grep, find, sed, curl, ssh) plus modern replacements like ripgrep and fzf to navigate and automate the system efficiently.

topics.label: Dotfiles
topics.desc: Version-controlled shell, editor, and tool configuration files (.zshrc, .gitconfig) kept in a repo so a personalized environment can be reproduced on any machine.

topics.label: Node Version Managers
topics.desc: Tools like nvm, fnm, and Volta that install and switch between Node.js versions per project, keeping toolchains consistent across machines and CI.

topics.label: .env & Config
topics.desc: Managing environment-specific configuration and secrets through .env files loaded by dotenv or built-in framework support, keeping credentials out of source code.

topics.label: Browser DevTools
topics.desc: The browser's built-in inspector for examining the DOM, styles, console, network, and storage, the first-stop toolkit for diagnosing frontend behavior live.

topics.label: Node.js Inspector
topics.desc: Node's built-in debugging protocol, accessed via --inspect and the Chrome DevTools or an editor, to set breakpoints and step through server-side JavaScript.

topics.label: Breakpoints & Stepping
topics.desc: Pausing execution at chosen lines and stepping through code while inspecting the call stack, scopes, and variables, including conditional and logpoint breakpoints.

topics.label: Network Panel
topics.desc: The DevTools tab for inspecting requests, headers, payloads, status codes, and timing, plus throttling, used to debug API calls and diagnose loading bottlenecks.

topics.label: Performance Profiler
topics.desc: Profiling tools that record CPU flame charts, memory heap snapshots, and rendering timelines to locate slow functions, leaks, and jank in the browser or Node.

topics.label: Console Techniques
topics.desc: Effective use of the console API beyond log, including table, group, assert, time, and trace, plus the debugger statement for quick pause-and-inspect debugging.

topics.label: Framework DevTools
topics.desc: Component-level inspectors such as React DevTools, Redux DevTools, and the Vue extension that expose component trees, props, hooks, and state transitions.

topics.label: Monorepo vs Polyrepo
topics.desc: The architectural choice between one repository holding many packages versus separate repos, weighing atomic changes and code sharing against build complexity and coupling.

topics.label: Workspaces
topics.desc: The native multi-package feature in npm, Yarn, and pnpm that links local packages together and hoists shared dependencies, the foundation of most JavaScript monorepos.

topics.label: Turborepo
topics.desc: A high-performance monorepo build orchestrator from Vercel that adds task pipelines, dependency-aware scheduling, and local plus remote caching on top of workspaces.

topics.label: Nx
topics.desc: A powerful monorepo build system and toolkit with code generators, a project dependency graph, affected-only task execution, and computation caching for large workspaces.

topics.label: Lerna
topics.desc: An older monorepo tool focused on versioning and publishing many packages together, now built on Nx; still common for coordinating releases across a package set.

topics.label: Task Caching
topics.desc: Skipping rework by hashing task inputs and reusing prior outputs from a local or shared remote cache, the key speedup that makes large monorepo builds fast.

topics.label: Module Federation
topics.desc: A webpack/bundler feature letting separately built apps share and load each other's modules at runtime, a foundation for micro-frontend architectures.
